turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on in, love. I'll get your observations before the doctor. You look a bit pale, are you all right?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not, really. I'm wrecked the whole time, and I'm a bit worked up about it. Will she be long? I've the school run.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Not long at all. Arm out for me. Blood pressure is 118 over 76, pulse 92, oxygen 98 percent, temperature 36.7 degrees. Pulse is a small bit fast, I'll leave that with her.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 92 dangerous? I've been getting breathless just on the stairs at home. Should I be in hospital?
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): I wouldn't jump to that. Have a seat, she'll talk you through it. Dr. Brennan's just outside.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr. Brennan. I have the nurse's numbers here. Tell me what's been going on.

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Where do I start. Um, I'm so tired I could sleep standing up, the periods are fierce heavy, and I get out of breath doing nothing much. Is it all the one thing? I'm kind of panicking.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll take it piece by piece, no need to panic yet. How long have the periods been heavy like this?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): About a year, I'd say, maybe longer. I can't put a proper date on it. Last winter, or the one before, I honestly don't know. It crept up on me.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, so roughly a year, and the exact start is a bit foggy. When you say fierce heavy, talk me through a bad day.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm going through pads like nobody's business. A good few in the day, I couldn't give you a number, and there are clots, big enough ones. Not every time, but often. Is that me losing too much, could I collapse?
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Soaking pads and passing clots is exactly the sort of thing we take seriously. Do you flood through onto the sheets?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): At night, sometimes, yeah. I have to get up and change. Then I'm destroyed the next day. Is there something growing in there, my friend had fibroids?
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): One thing at a time. The tiredness, is it every day, or mainly around the period?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day, from when I wake up. The breathlessness is on a short walk, or the stairs. My sister says it could be the thyroid, there's thyroid in the family, our aunt had it. Do you think it's that, she was on tablets for life?

[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thyroid can certainly make you tired, so it's on my list, but heavy bleeding plus breathlessness makes me think of the iron first, if I'm thinking out loud. Anything else you've noticed, the hair, the skin, the nails?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): The hair, yes. Well, actually, it's coming out in the shower, handfuls nearly. I noticed it since around the summer, or after, I can't remember which. Will it grow back, I'm really self-conscious?
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it's the iron, the hair usually does come back, but it takes months, not days. Are you on any iron at the minute?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I got Ferrograd in the chemist, the 325 ones. I take them sometimes, not every day. They can upset my stomach, or I just forget. Am I making myself worse?
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sometimes is a bit vague for me. Are we talking most days, or the odd one?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I genuinely couldn't tell you. Some weeks the box doesn't even open. I know that's stupid.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not stupid, just means you're probably not getting the benefit. Anything else, painkillers, the pill, blood pressure tablets?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol now and again when the cramps are bad. No blood pressure tablets. I came off the pill years ago. Was that a mistake, should I go back on it?
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not necessarily a mistake, and I wouldn't restart it today without the bloods. Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of. Why, are you going to give me something new? Will I react?
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nothing new just yet. The breathlessness, any chest pain with it, a cough, or swelling in the ankles?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. No cough. Ankles are grand, I checked. So it's not my heart, that's the bit I'm actually terrified of?

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not hearing a heart story as the main event. A low blood count can make the pulse quick and make you breathless on exertion, which would tie the whole thing together. Let me listen to your chest and have a look.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. My hands are freezing, sorry. Is that part of it too?

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cold hands can go with being a bit run down, yes. Deep breath for me, and again. Chest is clear, heart sounds are normal, no murmur. The conjunctivae are pale, and the tummy's soft, I can't feel any mass.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Pale. So I am anaemic. How anaemic, do I need a transfusion? Please don't say hospital.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I can't grade it without the numbers, so no transfusion talk yet. My working impression is iron deficiency from the heavy periods, and that would account for the tiredness, the breathlessness and the hair. The thyroid stays on the differential because of your aunt, but it's not my first thought.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): So what do we actually do? Will I need a scan? If it's fibroids, is that an operation? I can't be off work.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not sending you for an operation. Today we'll do bloods, a full blood count, a ferritin, and thyroid function. The nurse can take them before you leave.
[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): I can, yeah, whenever you're ready. Three bottles, that's all.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Three? I get a bit faint with needles. Will you do it lying down? And what about the scan, are you booking that?
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): We might do a pelvic scan if the periods don't settle once the iron is properly on board. I'm not arranging it today. Let's see how the next while goes.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): And the Ferrograd, do I stay on it or change? If I take it every day will the stomach be worse? Should I take it with food, with tea? I've a hundred questions, I'm sorry.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stay on the Ferrograd, 325 milligrams once a day, but take it every day, not sometimes. With a bit of food if it burns, or with orange juice. Not with tea, the tea blocks it. That's the plan unless the bloods say otherwise.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day. Right. And if I'm still wrecked in a week, do I ring you? What if I flood worse?

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let's see you back in two weeks with the results. If before that you're breathless at rest, or soaking a pad every hour, come back sooner or go to the emergency department. Don't sit on that.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Every hour, God. And the hair, will there be any difference in two weeks? I don't want to go into work looking like this.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't be judging the hair at two weeks. Hair is slow. The visit is for the blood results and to see if the energy and the periods have shifted at all.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): If the thyroid is off, is that tablets forever, like my aunt? I need to know what I'm facing.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it's off, we talk about it then. Most of what I'm seeing points at the bleeding and the iron, so I wouldn't borrow that trouble yet.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): Right so, left arm or right? We'll have you tipped back a little so you don't go faint on me.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Left is grand. Just talk to me while you do it. Is it going to hurt?
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): Sharp scratch, then you're done. Press on that for me. That's the three bottles away to the lab. Doctor will have them for the two-week visit.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mind yourself on the way out. Reception will put you in for two weeks. And the iron, every day, not when you remember.

symptoms.name: flooding onto the sheets at night

clinical_assessment.assessment: Iron deficiency from the heavy periods, accounting for the tiredness, breathlessness and hair loss
clinical_assessment.basis: heavy periods with tiredness, breathlessness and hair loss

procedures_and_investigations.name: pelvic scan
procedures_and_investigations.indication: if the periods do not settle once iron is taken properly

clinical_actions.description: Full blood count
Serum ferritin
Thyroid function test
Pelvic scan if the periods do not settle on iron
Take Ferrograd 325 mg every day, with a bit of food if it burns or with orange juice, and not with tea
Come back sooner or go to the emergency department if breathless at rest or soaking a pad every hour
Hair regrowth takes months, so do not judge it at the two-week visit
Do not restart the contraceptive pill before the blood results
Follow-up consultation

The patient reported she has to get up at night to change because bleeding sometimes floods onto the sheets, and is very exhausted the next day.
Hair loss was noted to have started around the summer or shortly after, in addition to being current.
Current iron use is worse than 'sometimes': some weeks the Ferrograd box does not get opened at all due to stomach upset or forgetting.
The doctor advised not to restart the oral contraceptive pill today specifically until blood results are available.
Examination included that the pulse was a small bit fast per nurse comment.
